skill.name: discord-automation
skill.description: Automate Discord messages, channels, roles, webhooks, and reactions through Rube MCP with current tool schema lookup.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents through Discord automation workflows using Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The apparent Ruby or shell execution and system reconnaissance detections are false positives caused by Markdown tool names and a Discord quick reference table. The skill has an intentional external Rube MCP dependency and dual-use Discord automation capabilities for messages, roles, webhooks, and reactions. No prompt injection text or local code execution evidence was found.

remediation.suggestion: Document that Rube MCP is a third-party service and ask users to review Discord scopes before connection.
Require explicit user approval before sending channel messages or DMs, and document consent and rate-limit expectations.
Require confirmation before role, webhook, member, or reaction changes, and recommend least-privilege bot permissions.
Treat webhook tokens as secrets, avoid displaying them in logs, and rotate tokens after exposure.

semantic_findings.description: The skill supports sending channel messages and direct messages but does not define consent, audience, or approval guardrails. This can enable spam, phishing, or harassment if used without operator controls.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The message and DM workflows are directly documented, and the file only mentions Discord permissions and rate limits. It does not provide consent checks or human approval requirements.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged Guild Administration Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents role creation, role assignment, role deletion, member update, webhook execution, and reaction deletion. These actions can alter access, impersonate via webhooks, or remove moderation signals if run without explicit approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The listed workflows are high-impact Discord administration operations and the file identifies permissions but not confirmation gates. This is strong dual-use capability evidence.

content.value_statement: Discord operations can require many tool calls and exact permission details. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP workflows for messages, roles, webhooks, and reactions.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents to search Rube MCP tool schemas before Discord operations.
Provides tool sequences for sending channel messages and direct messages.
Covers role creation, role assignment, role deletion, and member updates.
Documents webhook listing, creation, execution, and update workflows.
Documents reaction listing and deletion workflows.
Summarizes Discord snowflake IDs, permission bitfields, pagination, and rate limits.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Discord or Discordbot connection.
Does not implement rate-limit retries or batching logic.
Does not verify user authorization beyond Discord permissions.
Can operate only within the connected account or bot scopes.

use_cases.title: Post Community Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and send approved updates to selected Discord channels with channel and content confirmation.

use_cases.title: Manage Event Access
use_cases.description: Assign or remove event roles after checking guild membership, role hierarchy, and required bot permissions.

use_cases.title: Connect Alert Workflows
use_cases.description: Create or use Discord webhooks for incident alerts, release notices, or external service updates.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Channel Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Discord automation skill to send this approved message to [channel name]. Confirm the guild, channel, and final content before sending.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Announcement Webhook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create or locate a Discord webhook for [channel]. Use it to post [announcement] after I approve the final message.

prompt_templates.title: Manage Event Roles
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the guild member [user] and assign the [event role] role. Confirm permissions and role hierarchy before making changes.

prompt_templates.title: Clean Up Message Reactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review reactions on [message link or ID], identify [emoji], and remove only the requested reactions after summarizing the impact.

output_examples.input: Send an approved release note to #announcements.
output_examples.output: The agent confirms the guild, channel, and exact message, then sends it through the Discord bot workflow.

output_examples.input: Assign the event-volunteer role to a member.
output_examples.output: The agent checks role hierarchy, identifies the member and role, requests confirmation, and applies the role if permitted.

output_examples.input: Create a webhook for incident alerts.
output_examples.output: The agent lists existing webhooks, creates one if needed, and reminds the user to protect the webhook token.

best_practices: Search Rube MCP tools first so the agent uses current Discord schemas.
Confirm guild, channel, user, and message targets before changing Discord state.
Use bot accounts with the smallest permissions needed for each workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not send messages, DMs, or webhook posts without clear user approval.
Do not expose webhook tokens in chat history, logs, or shared screenshots.
Do not use administrator permissions when narrower Discord permissions are sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill require Rube MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill depends on Rube MCP and an active Discord or Discordbot connection.

faq.question: Can it send direct messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents the Discordbot DM channel workflow and message send step.

faq.question: Can it manage Discord roles?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers role creation, assignment, deletion, member lookup, and member updates.

faq.question: Does it include Discord API schemas?
faq.answer: No. It tells agents to search Rube MCP tools first for current schemas.

faq.question: Can it create webhooks?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents webhook listing, creation, execution, and update workflows.

faq.question: What should users confirm before running it?
faq.answer: Users should confirm the guild, channel, recipient, role, webhook, and final content before any action.
